subject: Seneca — Priority throughput & error spike: tactical handoff
messages:
From: Lena Brooks <lena@senecasoft.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Seneca Ops <ops@senecasoft.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Dec 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden spike in errors + throughput drop for /v1/generate (region: us-west)

Monica —

We started seeing a clear degradation at ~07:50 PST: 5x error-rate increase (5xx) and tail latency spikes for our production traffic to your hosted endpoint (model: rwd-13b-v2). Our platform is core to our checkout verification flow; this is impacting ~30% of requests.

Key details:
- Error rate: baseline ~0.2% → ~1.1% in the last 20m
- P95 latency: 220ms → 1.6s
- Throughput: sustained drop from 240 TPS → 160 TPS
- Region: us-west (same as our pinned region)

We can supply logs and samples if needed. Can you triage and confirm whether this is a model/regression or infra? We need an ETA for a fix and an interim mitigation (circuit breaker / fallback to smaller model).

Appreciate urgent help — Lena

Attachment: samples_snippet.txt (text)
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 Dec 2028 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden spike in errors + throughput drop for /v1/generate (region: us-west)

Folks —

Forwarding Seneca's report (below). They are hitting higher error rates and tail latency with visible throughput drop. This is high-severity: customer impact on checkout. I'm standing up a short war-room — please treat this as P1 for the next 4 hours.

Ask:
- David/Karthik: Triage root cause (runtime, kernel, KV cache behavior, autoscale policy). Steps to mitigate immediately (list actions + owner).
- Marissa/Hannah/Grace: Customer comms + expectation setting; prepare exec one-pager.

Immediate mitigation options to evaluate:
- Temporary route their traffic to a lighter model variant (rwd-7b-quant) with deterministic fallback.
- Provision a short dedicated burst pool (1–2 GPUs) for Seneca for 90 minutes.
- Apply throttling at route-level and enable aggressive caching for repeating prefixes.

I've requested logs from Seneca (they sent a snippets file). Attaching request for full logs.

Attachment: seneca-logs-request.txt

Thanks — Monica

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden spike in errors + throughput drop for /v1/generate (region: us-west)

Short triage update — initial findings:

What we see (from metrics + partial logs Seneca forwarded):
- Large increase in token-length variance starting 07:46 (spike in average sequence length). This drove higher KV cache churn and forced lower packing efficiency.
- Runtime reported multiple "KV cache eviction" events around 07:50 which correlate with latency spikes.
- A subset of requests triggered a fallback to rwd-13b-v2-quantized-compat (a variant with different kernel path) which shows a higher 5xx rate in early handoff windows.

Immediate mitigations (we can do now):
1) Route Seneca to rwd-13b-v2-stable (a pinned variant without aggressive quant-kernel handoff) — low-risk config change, ~60s to propagate. ACTION: david.kim (5–10m).
2) Apply a temporary front-door rate-shaping rule (95th percentile cap at 200 TPS) to reduce KV churn and allow the runtime to stabilize. ACTION: karthik.iyer (5m).
3) Provision a 2-GPU dedicated burst pool for 60 minutes to cover peak traffic while we stabilize (manual provisioning + routing). ACTION: karthik.iyer + infra oncall (15–20m).
4) If Seneca approves, enable fallback to rwd-7b-quant for non-critical endpoints (checkout verification is critical; need customer sign-off). ACTION: marissa.cole to confirm with customer.

I'll start with step 1 immediately and post results. Collecting more logs now.

--
David
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 3 Dec 2028 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Seneca incident — exec summary & proposed immediate actions (for customer approval)

Team / Lena —

Below is a concise summary we plan to share with Seneca execs and our CTO. Please review quickly; if no objections I will send this externally and request sign-off for the dedicated burst.

Executive summary (one-liner):
- Degradation in throughput and increased 5xx rate observed in us-west due to runtime KV cache churn and an unexpected kernel-path fallback for rwd-13b-v2.

Impact:
- Customers: increased checkout failures affecting ~30% of Seneca requests over last 35m.
- Business risk: revenue-sensitive; recommend immediate mitigation to protect transactions.

Immediate actions we recommend (ask Seneca approval):
- Provision a 2-GPU dedicated burst pool for 60 minutes (estimated cost impact: $1,350) to stabilize throughput while runtime parameters are adjusted.
- Switch Seneca traffic to rwd-13b-v2-stable (no kernel handoff) for 30 minutes then re-evaluate.
- Apply temporary rate-shaping at 200 TPS to reduce cache churn; monitor for 15 minutes.

Owners & ETA:
- David Kim: apply model-variant routing (ETA 2–3m).
- Karthik Iyer: rate-shaping + provision burst pool (ETA 10–20m).
- Marissa Cole: customer comm and exec note (sending now).

Attached: action_matrix.xlsx (proposed timeline + rollbacks), seneca_malp_analysis.pdf (initial log summary).

If Seneca approves the dedicated pool, we will begin provisioning immediately and hold a 15m update after stabilization.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: action_matrix.xlsx (xlsx), seneca_malp_analysis.pdf (pdf)
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Brooks <lena@senecasoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 Dec 2028 11:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Redwood — Seneca incident: proposed mitigations and request for approval

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the quick signal and logs. Our team has run an initial triage and we have three low-risk immediate mitigations we can put in place while we continue investigating deeper telemetry:

1) Route your production traffic to rwd-13b-v2-stable (no kernel handoff) — expected propagation ~60s.
2) Apply a temporary rate-cap at 200 TPS to reduce cache churn and bucket spikes (will be removed after stabilization).
3) Provision a 2-GPU dedicated burst pool for 60 minutes to keep throughput steady while we monitor. Estimated cost: $1,350 for the 60m window, billed to your account under usage.

If you approve, we will start 1) and 2) immediately and begin provisioning the burst pool (3). We intend to hold a 15m check-in after changes to confirm stability and will provide a post-mortem within 48 hours.

Please reply with: APPROVE to proceed, or REJECT to decline the dedicated pool but ask us to pursue the other mitigations only. If you have constraints on changes to the model variant, mention them here and we'll adapt.

We know this is impacting critical flows — we will prioritize stabilization.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: proposed_timeline.pdf (pdf)
